FY27. TARIL’s Q2 FY27 performance reflects better execution, improved capacity utilization, 
and operating leverage across manufacturing facilities.



Units 5 and 6, marking the strategic entry into high-level infrastructure and high-value 
infrastructure segment  


August 2026 with execution scheduled over the next 35 months  


with deliveries planned within next 13 months; won a large order from Damodar Valley



a significant technical milestone that values our products, our ability to withstand extreme 
electrical and mechanical stresses under fault conditions, in accordance with the stringent 
international standards. 


next phase of the revenue growth. 


manufacturing base serving the region.

continue to remain on track with our growth plans for the full year.

backward integration initiatives, and maintaining disciplined and sustainable  ramping up our  
progressing our backward integration initiatives, maintaining disciplined and sustainable 
profitable growth.

supportive. India is witnessing a significant investment across power generation, transmission 
infrastructure, renewable energy integration and grid modernization. Emerging areas such as 
data centers, railway electrification, EV infrastructure, and energy transition projects are creating 
additional sources of electricity demand and, consequently, opportunities for the transformers 
industry. 
With our broad product portfolio, manufacturing capabilities, established customer relationship, 
and presence across more than 40 countries, TARIL is well positioned to participate in the multi-
year opportunity across domestic as well as international markets.

Mehul Shah: 
Thank you, sir. Good evening, everyone. I will take you through the financial performance of 
Transformers and Rectifiers Limited for the second quarter and the first half of financial year 
'27. Let me begin with our standalone performance for the quarter. During Q2FY27, revenue 
from operations stood at INR709 crores, 66% year-on-year growth and 27% quarter-on-quarter 
growth. 
Revenue growth during the quarter supported by improved capacity utilization and execution. 
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR114 crores, 203% Y-o-Y and 53% quarter-on-quarter

FY27. This reflects the benefit of higher operating leverage and improved utilization level during 
the quarter. 
Moving on our performance for the first half of the year. For H1 FY27, revenue from operations 
stood at INR1,268 crores, a growth of 35% year-on-year. EBITDA stood at INR185 crores, 47% 
year-on-year growth, with the EBITDA margin improving to 14.6% from 13.4% in H1 FY26. 
Coming to the balance sheet, our leverage profile remained comfortable as of 30th September 
2026. 
On a standalone basis, total debt stood at approximately INR575 crores, comprising long-term 
borrowing of around INR125 crores and short-term borrowing for around INR449 crores. The 
debt to equity ratio stood at approximately 0.35x, reflecting a manageable leverage position as 
we scale operation and invest in future growth. 
Standalone cash and cash equivalent stood at approximately INR77 crores as of 30th September 
2026. In addition, the company continues to have access to other bank balances and unutilized 
QIP proceeds earmarked for its backward integration initiatives, providing funding flexibility 
for the planned capital expenditure program. 
Working capital remains a key area of focus. As of 30th September 2026, standalone inventory 
stood at approximately INR654 crores, while trade receivables stood at around INR1,053 crores, 
out of which INR825 crores is current and rest is the non-current debtors. Net working capital 
days stood at around 154 days, comprising inventory days of approximately 93 days, receivable 
days of around 117 days, and payable days of approximately 56 days. 
The working capital cycle reflects the nature of the transformer business, which involves long 
manufacturing cycle, milestone-based billing, testing requirements, and project-linked customer 
approvals. We continue to focus on collection, inventory planning, and milestone execution to 
improve capital efficiency as the scale of operation increases. 
 
To sum up, TARIL continues to operate from the position of financial strength. The growth in 
revenue and profitability during Q2 FY27 and H1 FY27, together with a manageable leverage 
profile, provides a sound foundation. Our financial priorities remain disciplined capital 
allocation, tighter working capital management, and the timely funding of capacity expansion
